≺.justification: The reverse morphism representing the evaluation of a level by the entity below it (n-1), propagating stability downward.

⋈.justification: The composition of sequential levels (moons, planets, stars) into a continuous chain of gravitational dependence.

⊙.justification: The identity of a level's state, where the level recognizes its own position and stability within the cycle.

∈.justification: The split of a level's state into two arms: one evaluated by the upper level and one by the lower level.

∋.justification: The rejoining of the upper and lower evaluations into a single stable state for the level.

⊥.justification: The negative/counter state where the lower level confirms the stability of the current level, acting as the counterweight.

⊞.justification: The paradice where the system is both grounded and ungrounded, holding the contradiction of non-well-foundedness without resolution.

Rejoin the upper and lower evaluations into a single stable state for the level.
Compose the stable state into the orbital chain, moving to the next level.

Record the orbital period, fixing the state of the hierarchy at this point in time.

Compose the stable state into the orbital chain, continuing the cycle.
Recognize the self-stability of the next level.
Hold the circular paradox, maintaining the non-well-founded structure.
Record the orbital period for the next level.
Re-anchor the system at the galactic center, closing the cycle and returning to the boundary.
